messages:
sam_support: FYI - customer (AcmeRetail) opened a support ticket claiming our /batch-rerank endpoint is returning misaligned scores when they send multiple queries in one request. They say it worked before and started failing after a CSV import change on their side. attaching their minimal repro and response below.

sam_support: Customer repro (they sent as CSV->converted to NDJSON on client):
```json
{
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "text": "best running shoes", "candidates": ["candA", "candB"]},
    {"id": "q2", "text": "waterproof jacket", "candidates": ["candC"]},
    {"id": "q3", "text": "hiking backpack", "candidates": ["candD", "candE", "candF"]}
  ]
}
```

sam_support: Customer says our response looked like: (abridged)
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"query_id": "q1", "scores": [0.12, 0.07, 0.99]},
    {"query_id": "q2", "scores": [0.65]},
    {"query_id": "q3", "scores": [0.33, 0.11]}
  ]
}
```

sam_support: Note how q1 has 3 scores even though only 2 candidates were provided and q3 only has 2 scores but 3 candidates. Customer believes this is causing incorrect rankings in production. They also said they saw occasional 500s and some latency spikes during large CSV imports.

alex_k: Thanks, pinging eng. @sophie_eng @jordan_sre can you take a look? Two quick asks: 1) can we repro locally from the customer JSON/CSV? 2) is there any server-side flattening that could drop candidate separators when content-type is CSV/ndjson?

sophie_eng: Looking. First glance — this smells like a flattening bug in the client->server parser when lists are serialized and an extra trailing comma or empty row exists in their CSV. If the service consumes a flattened candidate vector and we reconstruct per-query boundaries using a cumulative counts array, an off-by-one or missing delimiter could shift boundaries, producing the mismatched lengths.

sophie_eng: Repro steps I just ran locally (python):
```python
# naive conversion that can produce an empty candidate row if CSV had an extra comma
import json
req = {
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "candidates": ["candA", "candB"]},
    {"id": "q2", "candidates": []},  # empty row introduced by CSV
    {"id": "q3", "candidates": ["candC"]}
  ]
}
# server naive reconstruction that uses counts = [2,0,1] -> cumulative boundaries ok
# but if CSV conversion drops the zero-length list entirely you get counts = [2,1] -> boundaries misaligned
```

sophie_eng: I forced the CSV-to-ndjson conversion to drop empty candidate rows and immediately reproduced the exact symptoms: scores shifted into the next query bucket. Server logs show: 
```
ERROR IndexError: candidate index 0 out of range for query 1
  at rerank_service.py:421
  request_id=req-6f3a
```

alex_k: Good find. @jordan_sre can you check whether our pipeline ever relies on positional reconstruction without explicit per-query counts? I want to see code paths that accept both CSV and JSON bodies. Especially the legacy CSV importer.

jordan_sre: On it. Quick note: the endpoint supports two modes — explicit per-query candidate lists (preferred) and a legacy flat list + offsets mode used by older SDKs. I suspect the customer triggered the legacy code path by sending a CSV-derived body without offsets header. That path expects an offsets array in the request. If offsets missing, it tries to infer and that code is fragile.

sam_support: Customer says they did not set offsets; they only sent CSV and our client lib converted it. They upgraded their internal toolchain recently which removed empty candidate rows. Customer is upset because rankings changed overnight. Also mentioned a billing spike because they retried requests when they saw 500s.

alex_k: Short-term mitigation options: 1) immediately return 400 if we detect legacy flat payloads without explicit offsets and more than one query (fail fast, helpful message), 2) add a server-side validation that checks sum(len(candidates)) == sum(offsets) if offsets provided, and rejects otherwise, 3) temporarily map legacy path to strict parser that treats missing empty rows as empty lists (safer). Which do folks prefer for hotfix?

sophie_eng: I vote for 1 + 2 as safest quick change. Reject ambiguous payloads with clear error so clients fail fast instead of silently misaligning. Then follow up with 3 as a compatibility layer in a minor release with feature flag.

jordan_sre: Agreed. I'll prepare a patch: validation in request parser + better error message. Also add a short detector that logs if batch_size > 1000 or total candidates > 10000 so we can correlate with their latency/500s reports.

deploy-bot: CI passed for branch fix/rerank-validate (build 4827). Ready for canary deploy to staging.

alex_k: @jordan_sre please create an incident-like ticket for the customer impact (billing spike + ranking change). Add repro steps and attach the sample CSV snippet. Assign to me for release approval. I'll run a quick canary in us-west-2 after deploy.

sam_support: I told the customer we're doing a canary and will push a blocking validation to prod in the next 2 hours. They asked if we can refund retry charges — finance flagged it for review.

sophie_eng: One more note — add unit tests for CSV conversion that include: trailing commas, empty candidate lists, and mixed newline styles. Also add an e2e test that ensures offsets inference returns 400 when ambiguous.

alex_k: Sounds good. timeline: jordan -> patch + unit tests (1h), deploy canary (30m), monitor (30m), then prod if green. sam, keep customer updated with the timeline and ask them to share exact CSV if they can.

sam_support: Will do. Customer sent the CSV via secure upload link already. I'll attach it to the ticket.

jordan_sre: Patch opened: https://git.redwood/inference/PR/1225. Adding changelog entries and a small metrics flag.

alex_k: Deploying canary now. tagging logs with request_id=req-6f3a to look for correlated errors.

deploy-bot: Canary deployed to staging (us-west-2) at 1890123498 by alex_k.

jordan_sre: Canary looks clean so far. No more IndexError in the rerank logs for requests with missing offsets. Latency normalized.

sam_support: Updated customer — they're testing their CSV conversion on our canary and will confirm shortly. They asked for a follow-up once the fix is in prod.

alex_k: If canary stays green for 30m, we'll roll to prod with the validation. Also open a billing dispute playbook with finance for the customer's retry charges.

sam_support: Thanks team. Closing this Slack thread once prod rollout complete, reopening if customer sees discrepancies after prod. :thumbsup:
